title: The Uncounted Vote
summary: The Red Talon account of how the Impergium ended.

claims.text: Red Talons teach that during the Impergium they culled humans without breeding with them, while other tribes formed around the humans they bred with.

When the Silver Fangs called a great moot to end the Impergium and agree a Litany, every tribe had to approve each tenet, but the great wolves were not yet seen as a tribe and their vote was never counted.
A Full Moon named Fells-Trees demanded to know why the wolves had not been asked and how the humans would now be kept in check.

title: Red Talons and the Breeds
summary: Why the tribe has no homid members.

claims.text: The Red Talons have no homid Garou; nearly all of the tribe holds that human-born werewolves lack a wolf's instinct and lean on easily fooled reason.
The tribe treats this as a mark of purity, though having no human Kin leaves it able to defend its lands only by violence.
Metis are not formally part of the tribe and are given to other tribes, though in recent years a handful have been accepted.
The Talons will not let their wolf Kin sire cubs for tribes such as the Bone Gnawers or Glass Walkers.

title: Lodge of the Predator Kings
summary: Red Talons who want every human dead.

claims.text: The Lodge of the Predator Kings wants every human on the planet gone, with no compromise and no human Kin; it believes humanity's chance to redeem itself has passed.
Most of the worst rumours about the Red Talons trace back to this camp, and its open slaughter makes the tribe a target for hunters of every kind.
Its members expect to lose and no longer care about the consequences, which makes them very dangerous.
